significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that, for content-identical numeral-heavy problems at matched accuracy, reasoning-token count rises systematically with numeral fragment count, together with the form-(ii) mechanism that a "fragmentation-sensitive length/difficulty signal read at the prompt boundary BEFORE reasoning begins" partially causes that inflation. This establishes both a bounded behavioral law and a causal mechanism, constraining expected compute under alternative numeral encodings and explaining one source of budget misallocation; test-time-compute work such as Snell et al.'s "Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters" and DeepSeek-R1 makes such allocation consequential, although the conclusion remains limited to numeral-heavy reasoning rather than a general law of reasoning efficiency. Verified false would distinctly rule out fragmentation-driven inflation at equal accuracy and its proposed prompt-boundary mediation, but would not resolve other causes of overthinking; after substituting away these specific claims, the topic alone would not earn this score, so the rating reflects the matched-problem fragmentation law rather than efficient reasoning's general importance.

reach.justification: The clearest handle is the ex-ante, training-free intervention "re-encoding the same numbers into fewer, cleaner tokens," which can be applied before generation and therefore gives inference-serving and evaluation practitioners an action window to reduce latency and cost rather than merely diagnose wasted computation afterward. The transferable relation is that greater tokenizer fragmentation predicts greater reasoning-token use at equal accuracy, so after inspecting a new model's tokenizer the claim predicts the direction of the effect, while the activation-space "fragmentation-length debiasing steer" would still require model-specific re-extraction. Scope is explicitly limited to "numeral-heavy reasoning, not all natural-language tasks," with possible null effects for clean single-digit tokenizers, but downstream uptake includes evaluation harnesses and systems that gate or ship inference; deleting the fragmentation-specific predictor and re-encoding handle leaves only the broad topic and would not preserve this score.
